headline: The desktop app's interface layer — theming, navigation, settings, dashboard charts, notifications and several dialogs — is largely present in the code, with 8 of 12 tickets backed by implementation and 4 that the review could not settle.
what_is_there: The code shows working dark/light theming with accent colours, a collapsible navigation rail with sub-tabs, a settings dialog covering provider/theme/language choices, in-app toast notifications, a model-routing on/off toggle, a smooth dashboard metrics chart, a full file-editing dialog, and an end-to-end permission request/confirmation flow. Several of these are only partially visible — for example the toast's auto-hide timing and the permission dialog's own screens were not seen, though the surrounding wiring is.
what_is_unclear: Four tickets could not be confirmed either way: the first-run welcome dialog with nickname/email setup, the workspace member-management dialog, a general "Update UI/UX" item, and a broad intent to improve the AI flows the core team actually uses. The last two carry no specific described behaviour to look for, and for the first two the files inspected simply did not touch those screens — this is not evidence they are missing.
suggested_action: Ask the team to confirm the status of the file editing dialog, which is marked To Do but appears fully built, and to attach concrete deliverables to the two open-ended UI/UX tickets so progress on them can be tracked.
